newsitem.title: UK: Christian Salvesen details special dividend.
newsitem.headline: Christian Salvesen details special dividend.

text.p: Christian Salvesen Plc, the British distribution and equipment hire group, said on Friday that it will pay a special dividend, by way of a foreign income dividend, of 34 pence per share, totalling 100 million pounds, on March 26.

In November last year the company announced that it would pay a special dividend of 150 million pounds and started the process in February of this year when it paid an enhancement to the interim dividend of around 50 million pounds.
The company said the the special dividend, which will be combined with a share capital consolidation, will be paid as a foreign income dividend (FID).
By paying it this way rather than as a normal dividend, Christian Salvesen will avoid writing off any advanced corporation tax (ACT).
FIDs were introduced by the UK government in 1994 to enable companies with high levels of overseas profits to pay dividends without the need to incur irrecoverable ACT.

"Today's proposals underline our commitment to delivering value to our shareholders. The payment of the special dividend as a foreign income dividend is a highly tax efficient means of returning cash to shareholders," Alick Rankin, chairman of the company, said in a statement.
Newspapers have reported recently that concerns over tax liabilities are thought to be troubling many of the 400 Salvesen family members who control 37 percent of the company's shares.

Salvesen moved to silence critics in November with its plans for the special payouts and proposals to demerge its Aggreko equipment hire business after the company rejected a 1.1 billion pounds hostile bid from Hays Plc.
The demerger of Aggreko is expected to take place in the second half of this year.
Shareholders must vote on the special dividend at an extraordinary general meeting on March 13.
